_what: Flip-flops that synthesis legitimately removes (constant, or never read), per design, so check_signoff.py can require an exact register count. Format: "<design dir name>": {"removed_registers": <int>, "reason": "<why those bits are dead by design>"}. The check fails when surviving sequential cells < RTL registers - removed_registers. Every entry needs a reason a reviewer can verify in the RTL. JSON has no comments, hence this field. Also "undriven_outputs": [<top-level output port names>] with "undriven_reason": top-level OUTPUT ports a design deliberately leaves unconnected; only Yosys 'is used but has no driver' warnings on exactly those ports of the top module are accepted, every other driver warning still fails.

user_project_wrapper.undriven_reason: Owner decision 2026-10-06 (learning build): tiny_ai_core keeps only the Wishbone bus and the interrupt, and the wrapper may not contain glue logic, so the GPIO and logic-analyser outputs of the fixed Caravel interface are left unconnected. Tapeout caveat: a floating io_oeb leaves the pad output enable undefined; before tapeout either drive io_oeb high and io_out/la_data_out low from the macro, or confirm every user GPIO is configured as an input in user_defines.v.
